'In 588, the Sasanians set out from Nishapur to confront the Göktürks in eastern Khorasan' under Bahram Chobin; the Turkic-Hephthalite forces 'conquer the city [Balkh] along with Talaqan, Badghis, and Herat' (page titled 'Perso-Turkic War 588–589', reached as First Perso-Turkic War; it does not number the war, while the Third Perso-Turkic War page speaks of 'the previous two wars' fought in Central Asia; the first version of the notes wrongly called this one the Third). Mirror of western-gokturks /ledger/2.
589: Martyropolis is betrayed to the Persians. 'Martyropolis fell to the Persians through the treachery of an officer named Sittas.'

589: Bahram Chobin retakes Herat and Balkh. 'In 589, the Sasanians re-conquered Herat and Balkh', crossed the Oxus and 'set the Oxus as the frontier between the two empires'; the war 'ended with a decisive Sasanian victory and the reconquest of lost lands'. Mirror of western-gokturks /ledger/3.

region.text: Dara, Martyropolis, the Armenian cities from Tigranokert and Manzikert to Yerevan and Ani, and western Iberia to Ardahan

ledger.note: 591: Khosrow II pays Maurice for his throne. 'Khosrow not only returned Dara and Martyropolis', the Sasanians 'handed over to the Byzantines many cities, including Tigranokert, Manzikert, Baguana' (Yerevan and Ani too), and 'The western part of the Kingdom of Iberia, including the cities of Ardahan' became Byzantine dependencies. 'Khosrow II gives the Byzantine Empire most of Persian Armenia and western half of Iberia' (infobox).
591: the Byzantine-Sasanian war of 572-591 ends in a Byzantine victory (infobox): Bahram Chobin is beaten at Blarathon and Khosrow II restored.
602: Khosrow II dissolves the Lakhmid kingdom. 'The dissolution of the Kingdom of Al-Hirah by Khosrow II in 602.'
602: the Lakhmid land is taken in. 'The dissolution of the Kingdom of Al-Hirah by Khosrow II in 602'; Cliopatria's Sasanian shape adds the Lakhmid shape in 602.

region.text: the Roman-Persian frontier from Armenia to Mesopotamia

ledger.note: 602: the war of 602-628 begins (the page dates the war 602-628). 'In 602, Maurice was murdered by his political rival Phocas' and Khosrow declared war; the first fortress taken was Dara, 'the capture of that important fortress in 605' (604 in the Roman dossier). Year moved from 605 to 602 by the reviewer (me-06-c review): the contest starts with the war, not with Dara's fall.
605: Dara is taken again. The Persians' siege led 'to the capture of that important fortress in 605'.

region.text: Mesopotamia and Armenia, from Edessa, Amida and Mardin to Theodosiopolis

ledger.note: 610: Roman Mesopotamia and Armenia fall. 'Along the Euphrates, in 609, they conquered Mardin and Amida'; Edessa 'fell in 610'; Theodosiopolis 'surrendered in 609 or 610'.

611: the Persians occupy Caesarea in Cappadocia. 'in 611 they overran Syria and entered Anatolia, occupying Caesarea' (Roman-Persian Wars page); the 602-628 war page has Priscus start 'a year-long siege' (linked as 'Siege of Caesarea (611–612)'). Mirror of eastern-roman-empire /ledger/74. Cliopatria's shapes hold central Anatolia only from 617.

612: the Persians leave Caesarea and Anatolia. 'Having expelled the Persians from Anatolia in 612' (Roman-Persian Wars page); the 602-628 war page: 'Shahin's troops escaped Priscus's blockade and burned Caesarea' (no year) and Heraclius 'returned to Constantinople in 612'. Mirror of eastern-roman-empire /ledger/75.

region.text: Syria from Antioch to Damascus, Apamea and Emesa

ledger.note: 613: Syria falls. Heraclius and Nicetas lose the battle of Antioch (613 on this page; 611 on the main page) and 'Damascus, Apamea, and Emesa fell quickly in 613'.
614: Jerusalem falls. The Persians and their Jewish allies captured it 'following a three weeks siege in 614'.

intersect.text: the Roman land lost between 612 and 617

region.text: Cappadocia, Galatia and Bithynia to Chalcedon

ledger.note: 617: the Persians reach the Bosporus. 'Chalcedon fell in 617 to Shahin'; Shahin took Caesarea Mazaca and Ancyra fell 'in 620 or 622'.
619: Alexandria falls. 'Jerusalem fell in 614, Alexandria in 619'; the Byzantine-Sasanian War page has Shahrbaraz invade Egypt in 618 and Alexandria fall 'after a year-long siege'.

region.text: Egypt up the Nile: the land Cliopatria's 623 shape adds

ledger.note: 621: the rest of Egypt. 'the rest of Egypt by 621.' Cliopatria's Egypt appears in the 623 shape.

region.text: Rhodes and the eastern Aegean islands

ledger.note: 622/623: the Persians take Rhodes and the eastern Aegean. Rhodes and other eastern Aegean islands 'fell in 622/623'.

region.text: Armenia, Lazica and western Iberia, recovered in the Caucasus campaigns

ledger.note: 626 (Cliopatria's year): Heraclius recovers Armenia and the Caucasus. The Caucasus campaigns ran 622-627 (main page) and Heraclius 'left Constantinople to attack the Persian heartland' on 25 March 624; the Constantinople assault began 29 June 626 and failed. The pages do not date the recoveries one by one.

region.text: Cappadocia, Galatia, Bithynia and the Bosporus shore (without the Caucasus strip the Turks hold from 627)

ledger.note: 627 (Cliopatria's year): Anatolia is free of Persian armies. The page dates only the Nineveh battle ('12 December', 627) and Heraclius's winter offensive 'Late in 627'; Anatolia's evacuation is undated. Reviewed 2026-10-19: 330 of the cells Cliopatria drops in 627 are Albania, Iberia and Dagestan, which the Turks and Khazars take (next event); only the rest is Anatolia.

627: Turks and Khazars take Derbent and sack Aghvania. 'Early in 627, the Göktürks and their Khazars allies approached the Caspian Gates at Derbent'; after Derbent fell they 'swarmed over Aghvania, plundering it thoroughly'; Tbilisi was besieged and 'stormed in winter' (627-628, no year on the page; the 602-628 page has it fall 'probably in late 628'). The 602-628 page dates the Turkic attack to 626 ('sending 40,000 of their men to ravage the Sasanians in 626, marking the start of the Perso-Turkic war of 627–629'). The page does not say the land was formally ceded; the region is Cliopatria's 627 drop of 330 cells of Albania, Iberia and Dagestan, split out of the 627 Anatolian loss above (the 626 Armenian loss of /ledger/81 overlaps it by one cell). Mirror of western-gokturks /ledger/8.

region.text: the Roman-Persian frontier from Armenia to Mesopotamia

ledger.note: 628: Khosrow II is overthrown (25 February 628) and Kavad II makes peace with Heraclius. Kavad 'made peace with the victorious emperor Heraclius' and it 'allowed the Byzantines to (re)gain all their lost territories'; the treaty is undated.

region.text: Rhodes and the eastern Aegean islands

ledger.note: 628: the occupied islands are returned under the peace. 'the Byzantines regained all their lost territories' (undated).

region.text: Egypt, Palestine, Syria and Mesopotamia west of the Zagros, and Armenia (without the highland strip the Turks hold)

ledger.note: 629: the Persians evacuate Egypt, Palestine, Syria, Mesopotamia and Armenia. 'Under the terms of the peace treaty, the Byzantines regained all their lost territories'; the page has no evacuation dates, Cliopatria draws them in 629. Reviewed 2026-10-19: 58 of the 62 cells of Armenia that Cliopatria gives to the Western Turks in 629 lie in this drop and are taken out of the eastern-roman-empire loss (next event).

region.text: most of Armenia, conquered by Chorpan Tarkhan

ledger.note: 629 (Cliopatria's year): 'most of Armenia' passes to the Turks. The Third Perso-Turkic War page has only 'In April 630, Böri Shad, determined to expand his control of Transcaucasia' sent Chorpan Tarkhan 'to invade Armenia' (infobox 627–629; no year for how long the Turks held it), so the page contradicts a 629 hold and the date stays Cliopatria's, as on western-gokturks /ledger/11. Mirror of that event.

630 (Cliopatria's year): Armenia and Azerbaijan are back in the shape. The Sasanian civil war page is silent on them (it mentions only 'Khazar raids on Adurbadagan' and minting at Nahavand); the western-gokturks dossier has the Turks give the Caucasus back in 630. Reviewed 2026-10-19: the Third Perso-Turkic War page does not say when the Turks left or the Sasanians returned; western-gokturks /ledger/14 (Arab-Khazar wars page) has Turkic control of Iberia, Albania and Adharbayjan c. 627-632 and Sasanian influence back by 632. The 630 return covers the Albania, Iberia and Armenia strips of the 627 and 629 losses above, 389 of the 410 cells.

region.text: the Arabian south: Yemen, Bahrain, Qatar and the Gulf coast

ledger.note: 632: Yemen, Mazun and Bahrain are lost. The Arabian frontier peoples 'had already asserted their independence during the civil war of 628-632', 'the disintegration of Sasanian rule in the Arabian Peninsula'. Cliopatria removes the Arabian south in 633 (Bahrain in 630).

region.text: the Sawad, southern Iraq to Ctesiphon

ledger.note: 633: Khalid ibn al-Walid invades Iraq. 'The first Rashidun invasion of Sasanian territory took place in 633.'

634 (Cliopatria's year): southern Iraq is given up. The page dates the first invasion to 633 and notes 'the Persians defeated Abu Ubaid in the Battle of the Bridge' (634 on the main page), so the loss is Cliopatria's reading.

region.text: Mesopotamia west of the Zagros, with the capital

ledger.note: March 637: Ctesiphon falls. 'Ctesiphon, the capital of the Sassanid Empire, fell in March 637', after al-Qadisiyyah (16-19 November 636, main page) and before Jalula ('In April 637').
637: the fight for Mesopotamia is over. After Jalula in April 637 'Yazdegerd III went to Rey and from there moved to Merv'.
637: the court leaves Ctesiphon for Rey and Merv. 'Yazdegerd III went to Rey and from there moved to Merv.'
638: Ahvaz. Utba and Nu'man 'forced Hormuzan into a peace treaty' in 638, which Hormuzan broke.

641: Susa falls. 'Abu Musa marched against the strategically important Susa in January 641, capturing it after a siege of a couple of months'; Junde Sabur 'surrendered to the Muslims after a siege of a few weeks'. Month (January, the start of the siege) removed by the reviewer (me-06-c review).
641: Khuzestan is lost with the fall of Susa (besieged from January 641 for 'a couple of months') and Junde Sabur.

region.text: the Median plateau around Nahavand and Hamadan

ledger.note: December 642: Nahavand. The Muslims 'defeated the Persians at the Battle of Nahavand in December 642'; Yazdegerd 'fled to different parts of Persia to raise a new army, with limited success'. The Median plateau is the reading.
643 (undated): Isfahan surrenders. 'The siege continued for a few months before the city surrendered', after Nahavand; the page gives no year.
648: Fars is lost. 'In 648, 'Abd Allah ibn al-'Ash'ari forced the governor of Estakhr, Mahak, to surrender the city.'
651: Khorasan is conquered. 'In 651 the conquest of Khurasan was assigned to Ahnaf ibn Qais'; 'No resistance was offered at Merv'; Sistan was first invaded in 650 and Yazdegerd had fled to Kerman.

region.text: the last Sasanian land, Khorasan with Merv

ledger.note: 651: Yazdegerd III is killed near Merv and the Sasanian Empire ends. He 'was killed near Merv by a local miller for his purse'; 'The Sassanid dynasty came to an end with the death of Yazdegerd III in 651.' The land passes to the Rashidun Caliphate (Tabaristan to the Dabuyids under a treaty).

wars.name: Battle of Hormozdgan and the fall of the Parthians
wars.outcome: Ardashir I defeated and killed Artabanus IV on 28 April 224 and ended the Arsacid line; he held Ctesiphon from 226.
wars.note: The main page adds that Ardashir took the Parthian western provinces; the east followed within his reign (to 241).

wars.name: Siege of Hatra
wars.outcome: A failed attempt about 226-227; the city 'did not fall until April or September 240'.

wars.name: Roman-Sasanian war of 230-232
wars.outcome: No territorial result: Persian attacks on Roman northern Mesopotamia in 230 besieged Nusaybin without taking it; Severus Alexander's 232 campaign 'ended without any positive result for the Romans'.

wars.name: Roman-Sasanian war of 238-244
wars.outcome: Ardashir took cities in Syria and Mesopotamia (238-240); the Romans retook Carrhae and Nisibis in 243; in 244 Philip paid 500,000 denarii in a hastily negotiated peace.
wars.note: The Ardashir I page has him take Nusaybin and Harran in 237-238; the Shapur I page has Shapur beaten at Resaena in 243, victorious at Misiche in 244, and Philip's peace place Armenia in Persia's sphere.

wars.name: Shapur I's second campaign (Barbalissos)
wars.outcome: Shapur sacked Antioch and Dura-Europos and annihilated 60,000 Romans at Barbalissos (253); he conquered Armenia and killed its king.

wars.name: Shapur I's third campaign (Battle of Edessa)
wars.outcome: Valerian was defeated and captured at Edessa in 260; Shapur took Caesarea and held Cappadocia and Antioch until Odaenathus drove him out.

wars.name: Palmyrene campaigns against Persia

zones.text: Osroene and the approaches to Ctesiphon

wars.outcome: Systematic Roman and Palmyrene campaigns into Persian territory forced the Persians out of Roman Cappadocia and Antioch.

wars.name: Sasanian conquest of the Kushan lands
wars.outcome: Sasanian governors took the title Kushanshah in Bactria around 230; Shapur I burned Begram and Taxila in 262 and claimed Peshawar.
wars.note: The page gives 225 in its lead and about 230 for Ardashir; the Kushanshah list gives Peroz I's reign as 245-275 against Shapur I's 240-270.

wars.name: Carus's invasion of Persia
wars.outcome: Carus 'launched a successful invasion of Persia, sacking its capital, Ctesiphon'; no territorial change on the page.

wars.name: Narseh's war and the Peace of Nisibis

zones.text: the area between the Tigris and the Greater Zab and the city of Nisibis

wars.outcome: Galerius defeated Narseh (298) and took his camp and harem; the peace gave Rome the area between the Tigris and the Greater Zab, Nisibis and control of Armenia.
wars.note: The main page dates the peace talks to spring 299 and puts the five satrapies 'west of the Tigris'; the Roman-Persian Wars page puts them between the Tigris and the Greater Zab.

wars.name: Shapur II's Roman wars

zones.text: the land east of the Tigris with Nisibis and Singara

wars.outcome: Nisibis besieged in 338, 346 and 350 in vain; Singara (battle of 344) and Amida (359) and Bezabde (360) taken; Julian beaten at Ctesiphon in 363 and Jovian ceded the 299 lands, Nisibis and Singara.
wars.note: The Shapur II page lists the Nisibis sieges and the 344 battle.

wars.name: Shapur II's eastern wars against the Chionites and Kushans
wars.outcome: Shapur II 'gained the upper hand' around 350; a prolonged struggle (353-358) ended in an alliance with the Chionites whose king Grumbates fought at Amida; Sasanian rule reached Taxila.

wars.name: Armeno-Sasanian War of 363-371
wars.outcome: Shapur II invaded Armenia after Pap's return; 'Persian forces were defeated by a joint Roman-Armenian army in 371'.

wars.name: Roman-Sasanian wars of 421-422 and 440
wars.outcome: No territorial result on the page: the first after Bahram V persecuted high officials, the second when Yazdegerd II raided Roman Armenia.

wars.name: Sasanian-Hephthalite wars
wars.outcome: A defeat of the Hephthalites in 425 and an alliance under Bahram V; Yazdegerd II's wars from 442; Peroz I's three wars from 474 ended in his death at the Hephthalites' hands in 484 and tribute 'from 474 until the middle of the 6th century'.

wars.name: Sasanian-Kidarite wars
wars.outcome: The Kidarites forced Yazdegerd I and Bahram V to pay tribute; Peroz I 'finally vanquished Kidarites in 466' with Hephthalite help and minted gold at Balkh.
wars.note: The main page has Yazdegerd II drive the Kidarites beyond the Oxus in 450.

wars.name: Armenian revolts of Avarayr and of Vahan Mamikonian
wars.outcome: Yazdegerd II 'quickly subdued the rebellion at the Battle of Avarayr' (451); Vahan's revolt of 482 ended with the Nvarsak Treaty of Balash (484), which gave religious freedom.

wars.name: Anastasian War
wars.outcome: Kavad took Theodosiopolis (502) and Amida (503); the Romans regained Amida and built Dara (505); a treaty of November 506 ended the war.

wars.name: Iberian War
wars.outcome: Iberia rose against Persia in 524/525; the Perpetual Peace of September 532 left Iberia Persian and returned the Lazic forts to Rome.

wars.name: Lazic War
wars.outcome: Khosrow I devastated Syria (540); Lazica went over to Persia (541); in 562 the Persians evacuated Lazica for 30,000 gold coins a year.

wars.name: Sasanian-Turkic destruction of the Hephthalites
wars.outcome: The Hephthalite empire was destroyed around 560; the surviving Hephthalite principalities stood under Sasanian suzerainty south of the Oxus and Turkic suzerainty north of it.

wars.name: Aksumite-Persian wars

zones.text: Yemen from Sanaa to Hadramawt and Aden

wars.outcome: Wahrez landed in 570 with 800 Dailamite cavalry, took Sanaa and made Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan a vassal; a second army re-conquered Yemen by 578 and made it a Sasanian province.

wars.name: Byzantine-Sasanian War of 572-591
wars.outcome: Armenia and Iberia revolted (571-572); Dara fell in 573 and Martyropolis in 589; after the 590 revolt of Bahram Chobin, Maurice restored Khosrow II and received Dara, Martyropolis, most of Persian Armenia and the west of Iberia.

wars.name: Perso-Turkic War of 588-589

zones.text: Balkh, Talaqan, Badghis and Herat, south of the Oxus

wars.outcome: The Turkic-Hephthalite forces took Balkh, Talaqan, Badghis and Herat; Bahram Chobin, sent from Nishapur, beat them, retook Herat and Balkh in 589 and set the Oxus as the frontier: a decisive Sasanian victory.
wars.note: 'The Perso-Turkic War was fought during 588 and 589.' The page is reached as First Perso-Turkic War but is titled 'Perso-Turkic War 588–589' and does not number it. Mirror of western-gokturks 'Turkic invasion of Bactria and Khorasan'.

wars.name: Byzantine-Sasanian War of 602-628

zones.text: the Roman-Persian frontier and the Roman provinces taken

wars.outcome: Dara (605), Mesopotamia and Armenia (609-610), Syria (613), Jerusalem (614), Chalcedon (617), Egypt (618-621) fell; Heraclius's counter-offensive from 622 and the battle of Nineveh (12 December 627) ended in Khosrow's fall and a peace that restored all lost territories.

wars.name: Third Perso-Turkic War
wars.outcome: Göktürk-Byzantine victory (infobox): Derbent fell and Aghvania was plundered in early 627, Tbilisi fell after a siege (probably late 628), and Chorpan Tarkhan invaded Armenia in April 630; the Turks left the Caucasus after Tong Yabghu's murder about 630.
wars.note: 'Hostilities were initiated in 627 by Tong Yabghu Qaghan of the Western Göktürks'; the infobox gives 627-629, but the page's last dated action is April 630. The 602-628 war page dates the Turkic attack to 626 ('40,000 of their men to ravage the Sasanians in 626'). Mirror of western-gokturks 'Third Perso-Turkic War'.

wars.name: Sasanian civil war of 628-632
belligerents: rival Sasanian claimants and provincial governors
wars.outcome: 'Over a period of four years and five successive kings'; governors proclaimed independence and the Arabian frontier (Mazun, Yemen) asserted its independence; Yazdegerd III ended the war.
wars.note: The belligerents are factions inside the empire; no second state is a party.

wars.name: Muslim conquest of Persia
wars.outcome: Iraq lost 636-637, Khuzestan 641, the Median plateau 642-643, Fars 648, Khorasan 651; Yazdegerd III was killed near Merv in 651.

certainty.note: The Parthian succession lands and the Roman Mesopotamian frontier have no treaty line; the Kushan frontier is the Kushanshah vassal border.

The Roman frontier is fixed by treaty in 299 (the Tigris and the Greater Zab), 363 (cession of those lands, Nisibis and Singara), 387 (partition of Armenia), 506, 532 and 562, but the pages name cities and regions, not lines, so it stays soft; the Kidarite, Hephthalite and Caucasian frontiers are soft throughout.
The 591 terms name the ceded cities (Dara, Martyropolis, Tigranokert, Manzikert, Ardahan); the 628 peace restored the earlier frontier without a recorded line. The Arabian frontier is soft.
The Arab conquest ran city by city; Yazdegerd's remnant has no fixed frontier.

notes:
Dossier written by me-06-c on 2026-10-19 from 14 pages (the page budget for 47 shapes). Every event cites one of them; where a page is silent the event is confidence 1 and says so.

ROWS. (1) Start: Cliopatria's row begins in 215 (Persis around Istakhr); the infobox dates the empire to 224 (Hormozdgan, 28 April) and Ardashir's kingship of Persis to 211/2. The dossier starts in 224 (Hormozdgan, 28 April): fx-36 moved it from 215 because the Kings of Persis page has Persis a Parthian vassal until 224 and the parthian-empire and persis dossiers now say 224; the 215-223 shape (Persis) is the persis dossier's land, and the rename at 224 is kept as the note of what the day changed. (2) End: Cliopatria ends in 643; Yazdegerd III died in 651, so identity.end is 651 and new keyframes 644, 648 and 651 draw the remnant from the Muslim conquest page (a reading: the page's chronology of the plateau is muddled).
